nodes.description: mapping(address => uint256) balances declared in StandardToken, tracks token balances of each holder.
mapping(address => mapping(address => uint256)) allowed declared in StandardToken, tracks spending allowances.
uint256 public totalSupply declared in StandardToken, total token supply.
string public name declared in ERC20Token, token name set to 'clay.finance'.
uint8 public decimals declared in ERC20Token, set to 0.
string public symbol declared in ERC20Token, set to 'Clay'.
string public version declared in ERC20Token, set to 'H1.0'.
Token.totalSupply() constant interface declaration returning uint256 supply (no body).
Token.transferFrom(address _from, address _to, uint256 _value) interface declaration (no body).
Token.allowance(address _owner, address _spender) constant interface declaration (no body).
StandardToken.transfer(address _to, uint256 _value): checks balances[msg.sender] >= _value and _value > 0, then subtracts from sender, adds to _to, emits Transfer.
StandardToken.transferFrom(address _from, address _to, uint256 _value): checks balance and allowance of msg.sender, mutates balances and allowed, emits Transfer.
StandardToken.approve(address _spender, uint256 _value): writes allowed[msg.sender][_spender] = _value and emits Approval.
ERC20Token fallback function () { throw; } rejecting all plain value transfers.
ERC20Token constructor: mints 1000000000 to balances[msg.sender], sets totalSupply, name, decimals and symbol.
ERC20Token.approveAndCall(address _spender, uint256 _value, bytes _extraData): sets allowance then performs a low-level external call to _spender and throws on failure.
msg.sender, external caller used as index into balances/allowed and as spender/owner in minting and approvals.
Low-level external call _spender.call(sha3('receiveApproval(...)'), msg.sender, _value, this, _extraData) with attacker-controlled callee and gas, performed after state write.
Arithmetic balances[msg.sender] -= _value performed without SafeMath in Solidity 0.4.4.
Deprecated throw statement used in the fallback function of ERC20Token to reject calls.
Parameter _to of StandardToken.transfer, destination of funds.
Parameter _spender of StandardToken.approve, address granted allowance.
Parameter _spender of ERC20Token.approveAndCall, also the callee of the low-level external call.
Parameter _value of ERC20Token.approveAndCall, allowance and transferred amount.
Parameter _extraData of ERC20Token.approveAndCall, arbitrary bytes forwarded to the callee.

edges.reason: msg.sender is used as the source account of balances in StandardToken.transfer; caller identity drives authorization.
msg.sender is used both as allowance owner and as spender in StandardToken.transferFrom.
StandardToken.approve writes allowed[msg.sender][_spender], keyed on the caller.
ERC20Token constructor mints balances[msg.sender] = 1000000000, privileged caller obtains the whole supply.
ERC20Token.approveAndCall writes allowed[msg.sender][_spender] and forwards msg.sender into the external call.
msg.sender is used as the key into the balances mapping.
msg.sender is used as the key into the allowed mapping.
msg.sender is passed as an argument into the low-level external call, and the caller controls the callee and reentrancy timing.

StandardToken.transferFrom reads and updates balances[_from] and balances[_to].
StandardToken.balanceOf returns balances[_owner].
StandardToken.transferFrom reads and decrements allowed[_from][msg.sender].
StandardToken.approve writes allowed[msg.sender][_spender].
StandardToken.allowance returns allowed[_owner][_spender].
approveAndCall writes allowed[msg.sender][_spender] before the external call, leaving state exploitable during callback.
